- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spider plants prefer bright, indirect light but not direct sunlight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overwatering is a common issue with Spider plants; check soil moisture before watering.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spider plants prefer a humid environment but can adapt to average humidity levels.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spider plants prefer temperatures between 65°F (18°C) and 75°F (24°C).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Feed Spider plants with a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer (20-20-20) during the growing season, diluted to half strength.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Remove yellow or damaged leaves from Spider plants to encourage healthy growth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Use a well-draining potting mix specifically designed for tropical plants for Spider plants.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Check Spider plants regularly for pests and treat with insecticidal soap or neem oil if necessary.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spider plants typically need to be repotted every 2-3 years.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Inspect Spider plants for signs of disease and treat accordingly.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should fertilize Lola once a month during the growing season and every 6-8 weeks during the dormant season.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User should dilute fertilizer to half the recommended strength to avoid burning Lola's roots.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] User can fertilize Lola more frequently if she is producing a lot of baby plants (spiderettes).
